summary.text: Tokyo is the capital of Japan and the country's most populous city. Its metropolitan area, which reaches into several neighbouring prefectures, is one of the largest urban regions on Earth.

facts.label: Status
facts.value: Officially the Tokyo Metropolis, it is the capital and most populous city of Japan.

facts.label: City population
facts.value: The city proper had a population of over 14 million as of 2023.

facts.label: Greater Tokyo Area
facts.value: Including parts of six neighbouring prefectures, it is the third-most populous metropolitan area in the world, with 33 million residents as of 2025.

media.alt: The skyscrapers of Shinjuku in Tokyo seen from the Bunkyo Civic Center, with Mount Fuji on the horizon.
media.attribution: Morio, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons — Skyscrapers of Shinjuku 2009 January.jpg

summary.text: Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea, and the largest city in all of Korea. Together with Gyeonggi Province and Incheon it forms a metropolitan area that holds more than half of the country's people.

facts.label: Status
facts.value: Officially Seoul Special Metropolitan City, it is the capital and largest city of South Korea.

facts.label: Population
facts.value: About 9.6 million residents as of 2024. The figure peaked at over 10 million and has gradually declined since 2014.

facts.label: Metropolitan area
facts.value: The Seoul Metropolitan Area, covering Seoul, Gyeonggi Province and Incheon, was the world's sixth largest metropolitan economy in 2022 and hosts more than half of South Korea's population.

media.alt: Junghwajeon, a traditional Korean palace hall at Deoksugung in central Seoul, photographed in daylight.
media.attribution: Eunmi Park, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

summary.text: Singapore is an island country and city-state in Southeast Asia, sitting just off the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula. It is made up of one main island and dozens of smaller islets.

facts.label: Official name
facts.value: The Republic of Singapore, an island country and city-state in Southeast Asia.

facts.label: Territory
facts.value: A main island, over 60 satellite islands and islets, and one outlying islet.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: About one degree of latitude north of the equator, bordering the Strait of Malacca to the west, the Singapore Strait to the south, and the Straits of Johor to the north.

summary.text: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth above sea level. It rises in the Mahalangur Himal of the Himalayas, and its summit lies on the border between China and Nepal.

facts.label: Rank
facts.value: The highest mountain on Earth above sea level.

facts.label: Height
facts.value: 8,848.86 metres, as measured in 2020 by a joint survey of Nepalese and Chinese authorities.

facts.label: Range
facts.value: Part of the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas.

facts.label: Border
facts.value: Its summit marks part of the China–Nepal border.

media.alt: Mount Everest and neighbouring peaks of the Himalayas viewed from Gokyo Ri in the Khumbu region of Nepal.
media.attribution: Rdevany, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons — Mt. Everest from Gokyo Ri November 5, 2012.jpg

summary.text: Hạ Long Bay is a bay in northeastern Vietnam, administered by the city of Quảng Ninh. It is known for thousands of limestone karsts and islets, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Northeastern Vietnam, administered by the city of Quảng Ninh.

facts.label: Name
facts.value: Hạ Long means "descending dragon".

facts.label: Landscape
facts.value: Thousands of limestone karsts and islets of various shapes and sizes.

facts.label: Wider area
facts.value: It is part of a larger area that includes Bai Tu Long Bay to the northeast and Cát Bà Island to the southwest, which share similar geological and climatic characteristics.

media.alt: Panoramic view of Ha Long Bay from Titov Island, with limestone islets rising from the water and boats below.
media.attribution: Taewangkorea, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons — Ha Long Bay in 2019.jpg

summary.text: Borobudur is a Mahayana Buddhist temple from the 9th century in Central Java, Indonesia. It stands in Magelang Regency, near the town of Muntilan and northwest of Yogyakarta.

facts.label: Period
facts.value: A 9th-century temple.

facts.label: Tradition
facts.value: A Mahayana Buddhist temple, also transcribed Barabudur.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Magelang Regency in Central Java, Indonesia, near Muntilan and northwest of the city of Yogyakarta.

media.alt: Buddhist monks walking around Borobudur temple in a pradaksina, the ritual circumambulation of the monument.
media.attribution: Heri nugroho, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

summary.text: Bagan is a medieval city and UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Mandalay Region of Myanmar. It was the capital of the Pagan Kingdom, and thousands of Buddhist temples and pagodas were raised on its plains.

facts.label: Capital
facts.value: From the 9th to 13th centuries it was the capital of the Pagan Kingdom, the first kingdom to unify the regions that later made up Myanmar.

facts.label: Temples built
facts.value: At the kingdom's height, between the 11th and 13th centuries, more than 10,000 Buddhist temples, pagodas and monasteries were constructed on the Bagan plains.

facts.label: Temples surviving
facts.value: The remains of over 2,300 temples and pagodas survive.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The Mandalay Region of Myanmar.

media.alt: View over the plain of Bagan in Myanmar, with temples and pagodas scattered across the landscape.
media.attribution: Corto Maltese 1999, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
